title: Fadnavis Says He Will Be Disappointed if Ramayana Does Not Win an Oscar
excerpt: Maharashtra CM publicly backs the film's Academy Award chances while inaugurating Prime Focus Studios' global headquarters at Mumbai's Film City.
body:
• Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said he would be "disappointed" if the Academy Award does not go to Ramayana while inaugurating Prime One, the global headquarters of Prime Focus Studios at Film City in Mumbai.
  • Prime One houses over 1,000 employees and anchors the worldwide operations of DNEG, the eight-time Oscar-winning visual effects studio producing the film.
  • Ramayana, directed by Nitesh Tiwari and starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, and Yash, is set for a Diwali 2026 release across 50,000 screens globally.
  • The film's English-language trailer, featuring AI-powered lip-sync technology, has already been launched for international audiences ahead of the global rollout.

Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has thrown his political weight behind the upcoming film Ramayana, declaring that he would be "disappointed" if the Academy Award does not come to the epic. Fadnavis made the remarks while inaugurating Prime One, the first phase of producer Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios campus at Film City in Mumbai.

A State-Backed Oscar Push

"I will be disappointed if the Academy Award doesn't come to Ramayana," Fadnavis told the gathering, according to Bollywood Hungama. The statement marks a rare instance of a sitting chief minister publicly lobbying for a Bollywood production's Oscar candidacy, underscoring both the scale of the project and the political capital Maharashtra is investing in its entertainment ecosystem.

The inauguration follows a joint announcement made during the WAVES Summit earlier, where Prime Focus and the Government of Maharashtra revealed plans to develop a global entertainment ecosystem at the heart of India's filmmaking industry. That vision has now taken physical shape with the opening of Prime One, which serves as the company's global headquarters and houses over 1,000 members of the Prime Focus workforce in Mumbai, anchoring operations that span more than 10,000 employees worldwide.

"I will be disappointed if the Academy Award doesn't come to Ramayana."

— Devendra Fadnavis, Chief Minister of Maharashtra

DNEG's Oscar Pedigree

Malhotra's visual effects company DNEG, which operates under Prime Focus, is an eight-time Academy Award winner for Best Visual Effects, with credits on films including Dune: Part Two, Dune, and Tenet. DNEG, in association with Yash's Monster Mind Creations, is producing Ramayana, directed by Nitesh Tiwari.

The film stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Raavan, Sunny Deol as Hanuman, and Ravi Dubey as Lakshman. Backed by a reported budget exceeding ₹835 crore for its first part, the production dedicated 600 days to post-production to achieve what the makers describe as unparalleled visual quality.

Global Rollout Already Underway

The Oscar ambitions come as Ramayana prepares for a record-setting global release. The film is set to debut across 50,000 screens worldwide during Diwali 2026, with a second installment planned for Diwali 2027. An English-language trailer featuring AI-powered lip-sync technology has already been released for international audiences, signaling the team's intent to compete beyond the Indian market.

Oscar-winning composers A.R. Rahman and Hans Zimmer are collaborating on the film's soundtrack, adding another layer of international credibility to the project.

Political Stakes in Mumbai's Entertainment Hub

Fadnavis's Oscar endorsement is not purely cinematic. Maharashtra has been actively courting the entertainment industry as a growth engine, and the state government's partnership with Prime Focus is central to that strategy. The WAVES Summit announcement and the subsequent opening of Prime One represent a deliberate push to position Mumbai's Film City as a globally competitive production hub.

For Ramayana, the political backing adds a dimension that few Indian films have enjoyed. Whether the Academy takes notice will depend on the film's reception, but the campaign has clearly begun — with the state's highest office already invested in the outcome.
